en.title: Resident Evil Remakes Unleash on Nintendo Switch 2 This Fall
en.summary: Capcom is bringing its acclaimed survival horror remakes to the Nintendo Switch 2, offering a portable way to experience iconic terror. Get ready to dive back into Raccoon City and beyond on a powerful new handheld.
en.body:
The chilling embrace of **Resident Evil** is set to return to Nintendo in a big way. Capcom has officially announced that three of its most celebrated remakes – **Resident Evil 2: Deluxe Edition**, **Resident Evil 3**, and **Resident Evil 4: Gold Edition** – are making their debut on the Nintendo Switch 2.

This move marks a significant expansion for Capcom's presence on Nintendo hardware, ensuring that all mainline **Resident Evil** titles will be available on the platform, including future releases like **Resident Evil Requiem** and **Resident Evil Veronica**. The digital versions of these highly anticipated remakes are slated for release on October 16, 2026, with physical editions following on January 29, 2027. This strategy aims to tap into a wider audience, bringing these critically acclaimed survival horror experiences to a new generation of Nintendo players.

## A New Era for Survival Horror on Nintendo

The Nintendo Switch 2 has demonstrated a remarkable leap in hardware capabilities compared to its predecessor, proving itself a formidable platform for complex third-party titles. The prospect of experiencing the meticulously crafted environments and heart-pounding scares of **Resident Evil 2**, **Resident Evil 3**, and **Resident Evil 4** on the go, with minimal fidelity loss, is incredibly exciting. While the absolute pinnacle of visual fidelity might still be found on high-end PCs or consoles like the PS5 Pro, the performance and presentation expected on the Switch 2 are reportedly fantastic, according to early impressions.

Nintendo has a storied history with the **Resident Evil** franchise, having hosted some of its most memorable entries. The original **Resident Evil** remake and **Resident Evil 4** on the GameCube are legendary, and titles like **Resident Evil Revelations** on the 3DS also showcased the potential of Nintendo hardware for the series. The return of these beloved remakes feels like a homecoming, offering a chance to revisit classic scares with modern polish.

## Fan Anticipation Reaches a Fever Pitch

For dedicated **Resident Evil** fans, the arrival of these remakes on the Switch 2 is a dream come true. The ability to carry the terrifying adventures of Leon S. Kennedy, Claire Redfield, and Jill Valentine in their pockets is an unprecedented convenience. The games have been lauded for their faithful yet modernized takes on the originals, blending atmospheric horror with intense action. Many are eager to duel Ganados and evade terrifying pursuers like Nemesis while commuting or during breaks, a testament to the enduring appeal of these titles and the growing power of Nintendo's portable offerings.

## What's Next for the Undead on Switch 2

With the digital release date set for October 16, 2026, and physical copies arriving in early 2027, fans have a clear timeline to mark their calendars. The successful launch of these remakes will likely pave the way for even more Capcom titles to find a home on the Switch 2, solidifying its position as a versatile gaming platform. The journey through Raccoon City and beyond is about to become more accessible than ever.

content_raw: I’ve played Resident Evil about as much as any franchise in my life, which means I’ve replayed all of them many times over. As you may imagine, I jumped at the opportunity for more when Capcom wished to send me early access codes to review the Switch 2 versions of Resident Evil’s excellent remake trilogy, and I’m happy to say that these games all look and run fantastically on Nintendo’s handheld hybrid console. Image via Capcom Resident Evil 4: Gold Edition, Resident Evil 3, and Resident Evil 2: Deluxe Edition are all exemplary on the Switch 2 hardware, which shouldn’t be surprising anymore. Nintendo’s new console has shown it can stand toe-to-toe as a machine that plays all sorts of third-party titles, which is a far departure from the Switch 1. Having the remake trilogy on Switch 2 now means all mainline Resident Evil titles are here on Switch 2, and that includes Resident Evil Requiem and next year’s Resident Evil Veronica, too. The ability to take these classics on the go just makes it that much more impressive, because there’s not much fidelity loss in handheld mode at all. The best way to play these games will still be on a suped-up gaming PC or even a PS5 Pro, but having the franchise back on Nintendo and looking this good was unheard of just a few years ago. I’m of the belief that Nintendo has been home to some of the franchise’s best moments, including the original RE1 remake and original Resident Evil 4 on GameCube, the light-gun Chronicles games on Wii, and even Resident Evil Revelations on 3DS. It feels good to have them back on Nintendo again. Jumping back into Raccoon City and dueling with Ganados all over again on the Switch 2 felt really smooth, especially with the Pro Controller. Playing in handheld mode is a bit different and less enjoyable, as I prefer a meatier grip when it comes to playing third-person shooters, but it’s still worth it. Image via Capcom There’s definitely a bit less visual fidelity when it comes to certain textures, but unless you’re playing it side-by-side with the PC or even the Xbox Series X version, you shouldn’t be able to tell too much of a difference. The Switch 2 versions offer HDR and motion controls on top of what you may already expect, too, so if you feel like it, you can even use the JoyCons to gun down zombies (not my cup of tea, personally) to your heart’s content. The most important thing, to me, is that the games feel smooth at a solid 60 FPS with DLSS helping out with upscaling. They look and play great, as they should. All three games drop on the Switch 2 on Oct. 16, and they are discounted for the first few weeks: RE4 is 20 percent off ($39.99), RE3 is 33 percent off ($19.79), and RE2 is 25 percent off ($29.99), so I can wholly recommend picking these up if you haven’t played them already (and even still if you already have).
